question: Is the existing 2g deletion-witness bound improvable when all evidence counts and both predicted outcomes are positive?
construction: Two disjoint groups X,Y of g sources. Split subset monomials in each group by parity: P=even(X), Q=odd(X), R=odd(Y), S=even(Y). Raw two-outcome counts are (P+R,Q+R) and (P+S,Q+S). Apply the common positive mixing matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]. Each record uses at most g sources. Empty supports are permitted by the existing Profile contract and represent explicit retained background evidence.
prediction: Both profiles remain known with strictly positive outcome counts for every withdrawal. Their normalized predictions differ only when all 2g sources are withdrawn. Their first-outcome cross difference is exactly 3*product(1-x_i). Thus 2g is tight within this positive-count family; uniform random Boolean testing differs with probability exactly 2^(-2g).
cohort: g=1..6, all 2^(2g) withdrawal masks, no excluded case. For g=1..3 also use the unchanged existing Profile equivalence checker, whose width limit is 3; do not change that limit to fit the experiment. Above it, verify record readouts and canonical polynomial coefficients directly. Also test g=1..5 with one common withdrawable anchor added to every support: no empty supports, width g+1, first difference at 2g withdrawals while retaining the anchor.
control: Independent integer/Fraction enumeration of records, a closed-form parity-count oracle, unchanged Boolean cross-product and witness functions, and existing Profile equivalence where supported. The anchored cases must return unknown on both sides whenever their anchor is withdrawn.
gate: Every coefficient and every readout must agree with the proof, including the unique minimal counterexample. Test construction and withdrawal boundary validation. Preserve any failure; no parameter or cohort replacement.
claims: A sharpness analysis for the declared predictive-memory contract. It is not a storage, latency, answer-quality or system-superiority result. The polynomial-degree argument is established mathematics; a novelty claim needs a broader literature comparison. No paid calls or held-out task data.
